signals.title: CAD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + ESI Divergence
signals.text: CAD/JPY price action is anchored by a 1.415% G10 weekly performance spread, marking a significant divergence between the week's strongest and weakest currencies. CAD strength is supported by a positive ESI of +11.6, reflecting sustained data outperformance, while JPY remains the G10 laggard despite its own positive ESI of +16.3. The 125bp CORRA-TONA OIS carry differential provides a structural tailwind for CAD/JPY, which remains dominant while the VIX sits at 14.6 (low volatility). JPY speculative positioning remains heavily net short at -63,633, suggesting the carry trade is still the primary driver over safe-haven demand. Technical positioning for the CAD leg shows USD/CAD holding below its SMA20/50 cluster (1.4033/1.4075), confirming broad CAD resilience. Trade bias: Long CAD/JPY; carry advantage and data outperformance favor continued CAD leadership. Catalyst: next BoC meeting 9 Sep — hold priced. Risk: VIX spike above 25 triggers a disorderly unwind of the crowded JPY short position.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Complacency vs Intervention Risk
signals.text: USD/JPY at 159.30 is testing the critical 160.00 psychological handle, a level historically associated with BoJ verbal warnings and potential intervention. The options market displays unusual complacency with a negative Vol Risk Premium of -1.5%, as IV at 7.2% sits below the realized HV30 of 8.7%. However, the 25d Risk Reversal at -2.07 shows a strong put skew, indicating that while aggregate vol is low, institutional players are paying a premium for downside protection against a sharp JPY reversal. This positioning reflects a market that is structurally long USD via the +275bp Fed-BoJ carry differential but remains hyper-sensitive to policy-forced repricing. A sustained break above 160.00 likely triggers a shift from complacency to high-realized volatility if the MoF steps in. Trade bias: Neutral/range USD/JPY; carry bid competes with immediate intervention risk at 160.00. Catalyst: next BoJ meeting (mkt: 57% hike priced) 18 Sep. Risk: confirmed BoJ/MoF intervention forces a technical break below SMA200 at 158.15.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Macro Surprise + Volatility Premium
signals.text: GBP/USD at 1.3501 finds support from a June GDP upside surprise, though TD Securities notes the impact on BoE policy remains limited. The pair exhibits an elevated Vol Risk Premium of +5.0%, with IV at 11.0% significantly exceeding the realized HV30 of 6.0%, suggesting the market is pricing in heavy protection for upcoming events. SONIA-SOFR OIS differentials are near neutral at -9bp, leaving the pair reliant on data surprises and technical momentum rather than carry. Speculative positioning is net long +39,039 (70.1% long), which aligns with the spot price holding above the SMA20/50/200 cluster (1.3369-1.3423). This combination of crowded positioning and high vol premiums suggests that further upside requires a significant hawkish shift in BoE pricing to sustain. Trade bias: Bullish GBP/USD; technical cluster support holds the trend despite high hedging costs. Catalyst: next BoE meeting 17 Sep — hold priced. Risk: softer second-half growth leads to a long-unwind toward the 1.3412 SMA200.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Retail Divergence + Technical Break
signals.text: AUD/USD is testing upside levels at 0.7063, supported by risk-on flows and a breakout above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.6933-0.7016). A sharp divergence has emerged between retail sentiment, where 77% of traders are short, and institutional COT data showing large speculators are net long +37,990 (72.1%). This institutional-retail divergence at the top of the range typically signals further upside potential as retail shorts are forced to cover. The +60bp AUD carry premium over USD (OIS basis) further supports the bid in a low-VIX environment. While US inflation data was unexciting, hawkish rhetoric from Cleveland Fed President Hammack provides a floor for the USD leg, keeping the AUD/USD move contained for now. Trade bias: Long AUD/USD; institutional positioning and carry favor the trend against retail fading. Catalyst: next RBA meeting 29 Sep — hold priced. Risk: RBA shifts to a dovish bias, erasing the 60bp carry advantage.

signals.title: USD/CHF — Negative Real Rate Compression
signals.text: USD/CHF trades at 0.8120, supported by the largest carry differential in the G10 space at +375bp (Fed vs SNB). Despite this nominal advantage, the SNB's negative real rate of -0.35% vs the Fed's restrictive +1.52% creates a structural divergence in policy stance that remains underpriced by the options market. IV for the pair sits at 5.7%, below the realized HV30 of 6.7%, indicating a negative Vol Risk Premium of -1.1% and general market complacency. The pair is currently holding above its SMA20 (0.8114), but remains vulnerable to any shift in global risk sentiment that would revive the CHF's safe-haven function. Speculative positioning is net short CHF (-12,207), which is modest compared to JPY shorts, suggesting less potential for a violent squeeze. Trade bias: Long USD/CHF; restrictive US real rates and carry advantage sustain the bid. Catalyst: next SNB meeting (mkt: 100% hold priced) 24 Sep. Risk: VIX break above 20 triggers a flight to safety, compressing the carry trade regardless of rate spreads.
